problem: End-to-end navigation models output actions directly, lacking interpretability, explicit 3D grounding and multi-step planning, while modular systems (LLM planner + grounder + navigator) are disjoint, cannot replan from feedback and suffer domain gaps between separately trained components.
motivation: Embodied agents need to explore large unseen scenes, ground task-relevant objects and handle long-horizon, multi-target tasks from partial online observations. Fully annotated data for planning+grounding+navigation is scarce, but large amounts of partially annotated data exist, so a unified model that can learn from fragmented labels is attractive.
key_idea: Unify planning, 3D grounding, waypoint navigation and answering in a single autoregressive 3D-VLM that emits a chain-of-thought with a CoT-memory feedback loop, trained with a masked autoregressive loss that lets partially annotated samples implicitly supervise the other CoT components.
insight: Training only on fully annotated planning data (types 1-3) drops R2R-CE SR from 61.3 to 46.2, while removing planning data keeps navigation (60.8 SR) but t-ACC on SG3D falls from 9.3 to 5.3, so massive partial data gives navigation and scarce gold data gives planning. Removing CoT Memory drops R2R-CE SR 61.3->56.5 and SG3D t-ACC 9.3->4.1, showing the stateful feedback loop matters most for long-horizon tasks. Text-based actions instead of waypoints cost ~5 SR points, showing alignment with the 3D token space helps.
method: Multi-level 3D perception: Dynam3D encoder turns streaming posed RGB-D into panoramic patch tokens, instance tokens and zone tokens (feature fields), projected into the VLM latent space
Waypoint-based action space: a transformer waypoint predictor (12 queries at 30° spacing) proposes candidate waypoints; the model selects one or <navigation_stop>
Unified 3D spatial embedding: token/waypoint coordinates are transformed to the agent-centric frame; (P, distance, cos θ, sin θ) go through an MLP spatial encoder to align tokens and waypoints

Dynamic 3D CoT: NVILA-Lite-2B autoregressively generates plan text, grounded <target> pointing to 3D tokens (or <grounding_none>) via dot-product grounding head, waypoint selection via navigation head, and answer text; 'reached the subgoal' marks progress
CoT Memory feedback: parsed plans, grounded targets and traversed waypoints are appended to context (C_t = Concat(C_{t-1}, Parse(S_t))) enabling replanning when grounding or navigation fails

SLFS with masked autoregressive loss: 10M-sample hybrid dataset (175K gold, 9.9M partial); missing CoT components are generated but masked from the cross-entropy, so gradients flow through the shared VLM
Training: online simulator training with DAgger, sampling type 1-3 / 4-5 / 6 data ~1:1:1; 100K episodes (~14 days) on 4 RTX 6000 Ada

setting.training_data: 10M hybrid samples from ~5K real scans and 20K synthetic scenes: SG3D, Grounded 3D-LLM, VLN-Trans (planning); SceneVerse, MMScan, PQ3D (grounding); HM3D/MP3D/HSSD/ProcTHOR (OVON-style grounding-nav); R2R-CE, REVERIE-CE, SRDF, NavRAG (VLN); 175K fully annotated
setting.observation: streaming posed RGB-D (monocular camera) building a multi-level 3D memory
setting.action_space: predicted candidate waypoints (select one or stop) executed by an action controller
setting.privileged: none for navigation (posed RGB-D assumed); on SG3D the ground-truth planning text is given as input

results: D3D-VLP sets SOTA on R2R-CE (61.3 SR / 56.1 SPL), beating StreamVLN (+4.4 SR) and the modular InternVLA-N1 (+3.1 SR), and improving over Dynam3D by +8.4 SR. On HM3D-OVON it reaches 47.3 SR (best SR; NavFoM has higher SPL 31.3), and on SG3D t-ACC 9.3 vs 4.2 for Dynam3D-VisTA. In real-world mobile manipulation it completes 3/10 tasks versus 1/10 for Dynam3D+OWLv2 and 0/10 for OK-Robot and DynaMem.
limitations: SLFS relies on implicit gradient signals for unlabeled CoT components, and autoregressive CoT generation shows limited exploration; RL is suggested as future work
Training is expensive (~14 days on 4 GPUs) and could use only part of the 10M dataset due to compute limits
SG3D evaluation uses the ground-truth plan text as input, and the real-world test is small (10 tasks)
